    The last inequality is due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound}. 
                
                
                Rearranging the above inequality concludes the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the theorem's bound fails at $S_j$, then Lemma 6 and rearranging give the gap bound.

nodes.name: Trivial case
nodes.statement:
Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A$, Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained} holds immediately.
nodes.statement_short: If $S_j$ already meets the bound, the theorem holds.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
Hence, we consider the opposite case:
    \begin{align*}
    f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &\leq f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A\\
    
    
    &=f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j\\
    &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j .
    \end{align*}
  
    The last inequality is due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound}. 
                
                
                Rearranging the above inequality concludes the proof of the corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise chain the inequality with Lemma 6 and rearrange.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $f(S_t)-c(S_t)$ (Case 2.2)
nodes.statement:
Under the case 2.2,

the following holds:
    \[
    f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A
    \]
nodes.label: lem:unconstrained-h_St

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement:
Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) =f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) \!-\! f(S_{t-1}) \big ) +f(S_{t-1})\!-\!c(S_t)\\
    
    
    &= { \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \big )}  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}. 
\end{align*}
The first inequality holds from Lemma \ref{lem:marginal-gain}. The equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

Proceeding further from the above inequality, 
\[
\begin{array}{rl}
& f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
                &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\right)}+ f(S_{t-1})  \\
                &\hfill  + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
                 
                & \hfill- \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
                 
                &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{\mbox{\tt apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound}}}   \\
                 
                &\hfill + \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
                    &\hfill- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\big(c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\big)}\\   
                &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) (f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})) - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
                &\hfill + \underbrace{\left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)}_{\mbox{\tt residual value }}. 
\end{array}
\]

Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 



the residual value is non-negative. Hence, 
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $f(S_t)-c(S_t)$ with Lemma 2, regroup via $B_{t-1}$, apply Lemma 6; the residual is nonnegative by Claim 5 and Corollary 7.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2
nodes.statement:
Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) =f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) \!-\! f(S_{t-1}) \big ) +f(S_{t-1})\!-\!c(S_t)\\
    
    
    &= { \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \big )}  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}. 
\end{align*}
The first inequality holds from Lemma \ref{lem:marginal-gain}. The equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $f(S_t)-c(S_t)$, apply Lemma 2 and rewrite with $B_{t-1}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
Proceeding further from the above inequality, 
\[
\begin{array}{rl}
& f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
                &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\right)}+ f(S_{t-1})  \\
                &\hfill  + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
                 
                & \hfill- \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
                 
                &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{\mbox{\tt apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound}}}   \\
                 
                &\hfill + \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
                    &\hfill- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\big(c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\big)}\\   
                &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) (f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})) - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
                &\hfill + \underbrace{\left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)}_{\mbox{\tt residual value }}. 
\end{array}
\]
nodes.statement_short: Regroup terms and apply Lemma 6, leaving a residual term.

nodes.name: Residual nonnegative
nodes.statement_short: Claim 5 and Corollary 7 make the residual nonnegative, concluding.

nodes.name: Running time of UP
nodes.statement:
The time complexity of Algorithm \ref{alg:up} is 
    
    $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon} \log \frac{n}{\epsilon \gamma})$.
conclusions:
The time complexity of Algorithm \ref{alg:up} is 
    
    $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon} \log \frac{n}{\epsilon \gamma})$.
nodes.label: lem:time

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement: As per line 18 of Algorithm \ref{alg:up}, each element $e \in V$ can be evaluated for at most $(\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon})/{\epsilon}$ times. Each such consideration involves one oracle call to the function $f$. Therefore, the maximal total number of oracle calls for $n$ elements is $n \cdot (\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon})/{\epsilon} \in \mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon} \log \frac{n}{\epsilon \gamma})$.
nodes.statement_short: Each element is evaluated at most $\log(n/\gamma\epsilon)/\epsilon$ times, one oracle call each.

nodes.name: Approximation guarantee of UP with approximate oracles (RUASM)
assumptions: the input utility function is $\delta$-approximate to a monotone $\gamma$-submodular set function $f$
nodes.statement_short: With a $\delta$-approximate oracle, UP loses an extra additive $2\delta(\beta+n/\gamma+1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta')$ relative to Theorem 1.
nodes.label: th:unconstrained-approx

nodes.name: Theorem 10 generalizes Theorem 1 and ROI
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained-approx} generalizes both Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained} (with $\delta=0$) and ROI \cite{jin2021unconstrained} (with $\delta=0$ and $\epsilon=0$).

nodes.name: Modified ROI reduces to ROI for submodular f
nodes.statement: We notice that when the function $f$ is submodular ($\gamma=1$), the approximation reduces to the approximation result of ROI \cite{jin2021unconstrained}.

nodes.name: Diffusion model
nodes.statement: The diffusion model \cite{kempe2003maximizing} is defined using a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a probability function $p(u,v), \forall (u,v)\in E$.

nodes.name: Influence function $f(S)=\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{I}(S)]$
nodes.statement: A monotone submodular function $f(S) = \mathbb{E}[\mathrm{I}(S)]$ measures the expected number of nodes that are influenced by the set of nodes in $S$ based on a diffusion model, such as the independent cascade (IC) model \cite{kempe2003maximizing}.

nodes.name: Degree-based cost function
nodes.statement:
Following \cite{jin2021unconstrained, tang2018towards}, we use a linear cost function $c:2^V \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{>0}$ which is proportional to the out-degree $d(v)$ of a node $v \in V$. Formally, for every $v \in V$:
$c(v) = \lambda_1 \cdot d(v)^{\lambda_2}$, where $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are positive cost penalty parameters.
nodes.origin_citation: Jin et al. 2021; Tang et al. 2018

nodes.name: Profit maximization problem
nodes.statement:
Therefore, the {\em profit maximization} problem finds a subset $S$ of $V$ such that 
\[arg\,max_{S\subseteq V} ~\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{I}(S)]-c(S).\]

nodes.name: Directed graph with vertex weights
nodes.statement: Let $G=(V, E)$ be a directed graph and $w: 2^V \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}$ be a modular weight function on a subset of vertices.

nodes.name: Out-neighbourhood $N(S)$
nodes.statement:
For a vertex set $S \subseteq$ $V$, let $N(S)$ denote the set of vertices which are pointed to by $S$, formally,
$N(S) \triangleq\{v \in V \mid(u, v) \in E \wedge u \in S\}$.

nodes.name: Weighted directed vertex cover function
nodes.statement: The weighted directed vertex cover function is $f(S)=\sum_{u \in N(S) \cup S} w(u)$, which is monotone submodular.

nodes.name: Vertex cover cost function
nodes.statement: We also assume that each vertex $v \in$ $V$ has an associated non-negative cost defined by $c(v)=1+\max \{d(v)-q, 0\}$, where $d(v)$ is the out-degree of vertex $v$ and the non-negative integer $q$ is the cost penalty \cite{harshaw2019submodular}.

nodes.name: Vertex cover with costs maximization problem
nodes.statement:
The objective of the {\em vertex cover with costs maximization problem} is to find a subset $S$ such that 
\[arg\,max_{S\subseteq V}\sum_{u \in N(S) \cup S} w(u) - \sum_{v \in S} c(v).\]

nodes.name: Bayesian A-Optimal design problem
nodes.statement:
Given a measurement matrix $\mathbf{X}=\left[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\right] \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$, a linear model $\boldsymbol{y}_S=\mathbf{X}_S^{\mathrm{T}} \boldsymbol{\theta}+$ $\zeta_S$, a modular cost function $c:2^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, where $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ has a Gaussian prior distribution $\boldsymbol{\theta} \sim$ $\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)$, the normal i.i.d. noise $\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \cdots, \zeta_n \sim \mathcal{N}\left(0, \sigma^2 \right)$, the objective is to find a submatrix $\mathbf{X}_S$ such that 
\[arg\,max _{S \subseteq\{1,2, \ldots, n\}} f(S)-c(S).\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose measurements $S$ maximizing the Bayesian A-optimality variance reduction minus modular cost.

nodes.name: Bayesian A-Optimality function
nodes.statement:
Here, 
$f(S)=\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma)-\operatorname{Tr}\left(\Sigma^{-1}+ \frac{1}{\sigma^{2}} \mathbf{X}_S \mathbf{X}_S^{\mathrm{T}}\right)^{-1}$ is the Bayesian A-Optimality function, which is a non-negative, monotone and $\gamma$-weakly submodular function \cite{bian2017guarantees, harshaw2019submodular}.
nodes.origin_citation: Bian et al. 2017; Harshaw et al. 2019

nodes.name: Closed-form marginal gain of A-optimality
nodes.statement: Moreover, the marginal gain of adding a measurement $e$ to $S$ can be efficiently calculated by $f(e | S)=\frac{||z_e||^2}{\sigma^2+\left\langle x_e, z_e\right\rangle}$, where $z_e=\mathbf{M}_S^{-1} x_e$ and $\mathbf{M}_S=\Sigma^{-1}+\mathbf{X}_S \mathbf{X}_S^T$.
conclusions: the marginal gain of adding a measurement $e$ to $S$ can be efficiently calculated by $f(e | S)=\frac{||z_e||^2}{\sigma^2+\left\langle x_e, z_e\right\rangle}$

nodes.name: A-optimal design cost function
nodes.statement: The modular cost of a measurement $e \in [n]$ is defined to be proportional to its $f$ value, formally, $c(S)=\sum_{e \in S} c(e) = p\sum_{e \in S}f(e)$; $p\in (0,1)$ is the cost penalty.

nodes.name: $\gamma$-Guess
nodes.statement:
As the submodularity ratio is not known apriori, we implemented the $\gamma$-\textsc{Guess} algorithm ~\cite{harshaw2019submodular} to \emph{estimate} an approximate $\gamma$. 
The algorithm executes Algorithm $\textsc{UP}$ or UDG for a total of $T=\lceil \frac{1}{\delta}\ln \frac{1}{\delta} \rceil$ iterations. At each iteration $r$, there is a distinct submodularity ratio $\gamma_r$. The algorithm takes this $\gamma_r$ for the solution set selection in Line 4. The outputs of the $\gamma$-\textsc{Guess} algorithm is the set with the maximum objective value and the total number of function call.
nodes.statement_short: Run UP or UDG over a geometric grid of guesses $\gamma_r$ for $T$ rounds and keep the best set.

nodes.name: $\gamma$-ROI (modified ROI-Greedy)
nodes.section: A.1 Modified ROI-Greedy for Weakly submdular $f$
input: utility function $f$, cost function $c$, submodularity ratio $\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Greedy by maximum density, adding while density exceeds $\gamma$; output the best prefix.
nodes.label: alg:roi-weak

nodes.name: Quadratic runtime of $\gamma$-ROI
nodes.statement: The algorithm will iterate at most $n$ times, and every time it takes $\mathcal{O}(n)$ oracle calls to $f$ to find the maximal density. Therefore, the worst-case runtime is bounded by $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$.

nodes.name: Approximation guarantee of $\gamma$-ROI (modified ROI)
nodes.statement:
Given a monotone $\gamma$-submodular function $f:2^{V} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}$ and a modular cost function $c$, after $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ oracle calls,  Algorithm \ref{alg:roi-weak} outputs $\Tilde{S}$ such that
    \[f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq \gamma f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})- \frac{1}{\gamma}A\]
    where $A = c({\rm OPT}) \log \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and ${\rm OPT} =  arg\,max_{T \subseteq V}\{f(T)-c(T)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\gamma$-ROI uses $O(n^2)$ oracle calls and gets $\gamma f(OPT)-c(OPT)-A/\gamma$.
nodes.label: th:unconstrained-greedy

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 12
nodes.statement_short: Adapt Theorem 1's proof: modified marginal-gain lemmas, then Case 1 directly and Case 2 as Theorem 1 with $\epsilon=0$.

nodes.name: Adapt Theorem 1's proof
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained-greedy} can be adapted from the proof of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained}. Next, we show how to modify some lemmas and results to derive Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained-greedy}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to modifications of Theorem 1's proof.

nodes.name: Lemma 13 and its proof
nodes.statement_short: State and prove Lemma 13.

nodes.name: Lemma 14
nodes.statement_short: State Lemma 14.

nodes.name: Split on $A$ vs $c(S_\ell)$
nodes.statement: Let $S_\ell$ with size $\ell$ be the set at the termination of Algorithm \ref{alg:roi-weak}. We divide the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-greedy} into two cases based on the relationship between $A$ and $c(S_\ell)$.
nodes.statement_short: Split into cases comparing $\gamma c(S_\ell)$ with $A$.

nodes.name: Case 1
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 1}: $\gamma c(S_\ell) < A$.\\
    Consider each element $u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_\ell$ that was not included into $S_\ell$, we have
    \begin{equation} \frac{f(u|S_\ell)}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma
    \end{equation}
        
    Therefore, for Case 1, we have
    \begin{align*}
        f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\!\!\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT})\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} c(u) \\
        &\leq 0 \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it follows from  Eq. (\ref{eq:o1-g})}\\
        &\leq \frac{A}{\gamma}-c(S_\ell)
    \end{align*}

     
     Combining the above inequality with the Case 1 condition ($\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell) < A$), we have 
     \begin{align*}
         f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S})& \geq f(S_\ell)-c(S_\ell)\\
         &\geq \gamma f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma}A
     \end{align*}

    {This concludes the proof of the theorem for Case 1}. \hfill $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Case $\gamma c(S_\ell)<A$: missed OPT elements have density at most $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Density of missed elements
nodes.statement_short: Missed OPT elements have density at most $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Bound the gap
nodes.statement:
Therefore, for Case 1, we have
    \begin{align*}
        f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\!\!\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT})\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} c(u) \\
        &\leq 0 \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it follows from  Eq. (\ref{eq:o1-g})}\\
        &\leq \frac{A}{\gamma}-c(S_\ell)
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Weak submodularity bounds the gap by $A/\gamma-c(S_\ell)$.

nodes.name: Conclude Case 1
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the case condition.

nodes.name: Case 2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 2}: $\gamma c(S_\ell) \geq A$. \\
    The proof of this case follows from the proofs of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained} with $\epsilon=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case 2 follows from Theorem 1's proof with $\epsilon=0$.

nodes.name: Marginal gain lower bound for $\gamma$-ROI
nodes.statement:
For all $1 \leq i \leq \ell$ and if $v_i$ be the element added to $S_{i-1}$, then
\[ 
f(v_i|S_{i-1}) \geq \gamma \frac{c(v_i)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{i-1}) \big ) 
\]
nodes.label: lem:marginal-gain-g

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 13
nodes.statement_short: Greedy choice dominates every OPT element's density; sum with monotonicity and weak submodularity.

nodes.name: Greedy density comparison
nodes.statement_short: The greedy choice has density at least that of every OPT element.

nodes.name: Sum over OPT
nodes.statement:
Since $v_i$ is added to $S_{i-1}$, we have: 
\begin{align*}
     f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{i-1}) &\leq f({\rm OPT} \cup S_{i-1})-f(S_{i-1})\\
     &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} f(u|S_{i-1})  \\
    &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} c(u) \cdot \frac{f(v_i|S_{i-1})}{c(v_i)}  \quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it  due to Eq.~(\ref{eq:i-2-g})} \\
    &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma} \frac{f(v_i|S_{i-1})}{c(v_i)} c({\rm OPT})
\end{align*}

The first two inequalities hold from monotonicity and weak submodularity (Def. \ref{def:weak-sub}) of $f$. Rearranging the last inequality concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity and weak submodularity then rearrangement give the bound.

nodes.name: Greedy density comparison
nodes.statement: \frac{f(v_i|S_{i-1})}{c(v_i)}\geq \frac{f(u|S_{i-1})}{c(u)}
nodes.label: eq:i-2-g

nodes.name: Lower bound on $f(S_i)$ for $\gamma$-ROI
assumptions: $v_i$ is the element added to $S_{i-1}$ in the $i$-th iteration
nodes.label: lem:f-Si-g

nodes.name: Product lower bound on $f(S_i)$ for $\gamma$-ROI
nodes.statement: f(S_{i}) \geq \left(1- \prod_{s=1}^{i} \left(1- \gamma \frac{c(v_i)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})
nodes.label: eq:f-Si-g

nodes.name: Density bound for missed elements in $\gamma$-ROI
nodes.statement: \frac{f(u|S_\ell)}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma
nodes.label: eq:o1-g

nodes.name: threshold-ROI
nodes.section: A.2 Threshold Greedy for Weakly submodular $f$
input: utility function $f$, cost function $c$, submodularity ratio $\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Global decreasing threshold greedy: add any element with density above $\tau$, decay $\tau$ by $(1-\epsilon)$ until $\tau\le\gamma$.
nodes.label: alg:roi-threshold

nodes.name: Approximation guarantee of threshold-ROI
nodes.statement:
Given a monotone $\gamma$-submodular function $f:2^{V} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{\geq 0}$, a modular cost function $c$, an error threshold $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, after $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log \tau_0)$ oracle calls,  Algorithm \ref{alg:roi-weak} outputs $\Tilde{S}$ such that
    \[f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})- \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A\]
    where $A = c({\rm OPT}) \log \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$, ${\rm OPT} =  arg\,max_{T \subseteq V}\{f(T)-c(T)\}$ and $\tau_0 = \max_{u \in V}\frac{f(u)}{c(u)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Threshold greedy achieves the UP guarantee with $O(\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log\tau_0)$ oracle calls, $\tau_0$ the max singleton density.
nodes.label: th:unconstrained-thresh

nodes.name: Unbounded runtime of threshold-ROI
nodes.statement: \textbf{\textit{Note that $\tau_0$ is unbounded since the density of an element can be exponentially large, so the running time of this Algorithm \ref{alg:roi-threshold} can be as bad as $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ or even worse.}}

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 15
nodes.statement_short: Prove the marginal-gain lemma for the threshold rule, then defer the rest to Theorem 1's proof and bound the runtime.

nodes.name: Proof plan
nodes.statement: The proof method of the theoretical bound of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained-thresh} is similar to the previous theorems. We first prove the lower bound of the marginal gain when adding an element to the seed set. Then, we prove the theorem by cases.
nodes.statement_short: Same plan as previous theorems: marginal-gain bound, then cases.

nodes.name: Lemma 16 and its proof
nodes.statement_short: State and prove Lemma 16.

nodes.name: Rest as in Theorem 1
nodes.statement:
\textbf{\textit{Notice that the above lemma gives the same property as in the proof of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained}. The remaining proofs of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained-thresh} are the same as the corresponding proofs of Theorem \ref{th:unconstrained}.
Therefore, readers can find the rest of the proofs in the main paper. We jump right to the running time analysis.}}
nodes.statement_short: The remaining steps are those of Theorem 1's proof.

nodes.name: Lemma 17 and runtime
nodes.statement:
\begin{lemma} The time complexity of Algorithm~\ref{alg:roi-threshold} is $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log \frac{\tau}{\epsilon})$. 
\end{lemma}


The for-loop runs at most $n$ times for each choice of threshold $\tau$. Let $\tau_0 = \max_{e \in V}\{\frac{f(e)}{c(e)}\}$ be the initial threshold. We know that $\gamma$ is the threshold at termination of the algorithm. If $T$ is the number of runs of the while-loop, then
\[
T = 2+\log_{(1-\epsilon)^{-1}} \frac{\tau_0}{\gamma} = 2-\frac{\ln \tau_0-\ln \gamma}{\ln 1-\epsilon}
\leq 2+\epsilon^{-1} (\ln \tau_0 -\ln \gamma) \in O(\epsilon^{-1} \log \tau_0)
\]

So, the overall run time is $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log \tau_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: State and argue Lemma 17 on the running time.

nodes.name: Marginal gain lower bound for threshold-ROI
nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 17
nodes.statement:
The for-loop runs at most $n$ times for each choice of threshold $\tau$. Let $\tau_0 = \max_{e \in V}\{\frac{f(e)}{c(e)}\}$ be the initial threshold. We know that $\gamma$ is the threshold at termination of the algorithm. If $T$ is the number of runs of the while-loop, then
\[
T = 2+\log_{(1-\epsilon)^{-1}} \frac{\tau_0}{\gamma} = 2-\frac{\ln \tau_0-\ln \gamma}{\ln 1-\epsilon}
\leq 2+\epsilon^{-1} (\ln \tau_0 -\ln \gamma) \in O(\epsilon^{-1} \log \tau_0)
\]

So, the overall run time is $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log \tau_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Count while-loop rounds of geometric threshold decay from $\tau_0$ to $\gamma$, $n$ calls each.

nodes.statement:
By Definition \ref{def:approximate}, we have, for every $S \subseteq V$ and $v \in V \setminus S$
    \[ f(S) - \delta \leq \Tilde{f}(S) \leq f(S) + \delta\]
    \[ f(v \mid S) - 2\delta \leq \Tilde{f}(v \mid S) \leq \Tilde{f}(v \mid S) - 2\delta \]
nodes.statement_short: A $\delta$-approximate oracle perturbs values by $\delta$ and marginal gains by $2\delta$.

\]
conclusions: f(v_i|S_{i-1}) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_i)}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{i-1})\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)

nodes.name: Sum and rearrange
nodes.statement:
Since $v_i$ is added to $S_{i-1}$, we have: 
\begin{align*}
     f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{i-1})  &\leq f({\rm OPT} \cup S_{i-1})-f(S_{i-1})  \ \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it as $f$ is monotone}\\
    &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} f(u|S_{i-1}) \ \quad\quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Def.~\ref{def:weak-sub}} \\
    &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} \left[\frac{c(u)}{1-\epsilon} \cdot \frac{f(v_i|S_{i-1})+2\delta}{c(v_i)}+2\delta \right] \quad\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it  due to Eq. (\ref{eq:approx-gain-approx})} \\
    &=\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \cdot \frac{f(v_i|S_{i-1})+2\delta}{c(v_i)} \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} c(u) + \sum_{u\in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{i-1}} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma}  \\
    &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \cdot \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c(v_i)} \Big[f(v_i|S_{i-1})+2\delta \Big]  + \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma}\\
    &= \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \cdot \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c(v_i)} f(v_i|S_{i-1}) + \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} \left( \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)} + n\right)
\end{align*}

Rearranging the last inequality concludes the proof. 
\begin{align*}
    f(v_i|S_{i-1}) &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_i)}{c({\rm OPT})} \left[f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{i-1}) - \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} \left( \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)} + n\right) \right]\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_i)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big[ f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{i-1})\Big] - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) 
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over OPT with weak submodularity and rearrange.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 20
nodes.statement:
We prove this lemma by induction. 


\textbf{Base Case: }
We verify the base case $i=1$ using Lemma \ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}; note that
$f(\emptyset) = 0$.

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_1) = f(\{v_1\})=f(v|\emptyset) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})} \left[ f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{0})\right] - 2\delta  \left( 1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &=\gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})}  f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)
\end{align*}
Since $c(v_1) \leq c({\rm OPT})$ and by the definition of $\beta$, $\beta = \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c_{min}}$), we have:
\begin{align*}
    1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} &\leq \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c(v_1)} \left[ 1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right]  \\
    &= \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c(v_1)} + n(1-\epsilon) \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c(v_1)}\cdot \frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})}\\
    &\leq \beta + n(1-\epsilon) \\
    &\leq \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}
\end{align*}
Therefore, \[f(S_1) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\]

The above inequality is consistent with the one that we plug in $i=1$ to Lemma \ref{lem:f-Si-approx}. Thus, we proved this lemma for the base case.


\textbf{Inductive Steps: }
For $i>1$, as an inductive hypothesis (I.H.), we assume
\[\forall j \in [1, i -1]:~~
 f(S_{j}) \geq \left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma})
\]
is true. We need to prove the inequality for $f(S_{j+1})$, 


    \begin{align*}
        &f(S_{j+1}) = f(S_j)+f(v_{j+1}|S_j)\\
        &\geq f(S_j) + \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \quad\quad\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}\\
        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) f(S_j) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) \right]}_{\mbox{\it by induction hypothesis}} \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \  - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT})  \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -\left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma})   - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\left[\prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]f({\rm OPT})\\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  \\
        &= \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]
    \end{align*} 

Next, we derive the second term,
\begin{align*}
    &\left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\cdot\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}  + \frac{n}{\gamma} - (1-\epsilon) n\frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} + 1 + n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})}\\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\beta  + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 \\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\cdot \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c_{min}}\\
    & = \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c_{min}}\\
    &\leq \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} 
\end{align*}

Thus, we proved for the inductive step,
\[f(S_{j+1}) \geq \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta \left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} \right)\]
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $i$ using Lemma 19. The inductive step shows the accumulated $\delta$-error stays below $2\delta(\beta/(\gamma(1-\epsilon))+n/\gamma)$.

We verify the base case $i=1$ using Lemma \ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}; note that
$f(\emptyset) = 0$.

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_1) = f(\{v_1\})=f(v|\emptyset) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})} \left[ f({\rm OPT})-f(S_{0})\right] - 2\delta  \left( 1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &=\gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_1)}{c({\rm OPT})}  f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_1)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)
\end{align*}

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Inductive Steps: }
For $i>1$, as an inductive hypothesis (I.H.), we assume
\[\forall j \in [1, i -1]:~~
 f(S_{j}) \geq \left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma})
\]
is true. We need to prove the inequality for $f(S_{j+1})$, 


    \begin{align*}
        &f(S_{j+1}) = f(S_j)+f(v_{j+1}|S_j)\\
        &\geq f(S_j) + \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \quad\quad\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}\\
        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) f(S_j) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) \right]}_{\mbox{\it by induction hypothesis}} \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \  - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT})  \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -\left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma})   - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\left[\prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]f({\rm OPT})\\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  \\
        &= \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]
    \end{align*} 

Next, we derive the second term,
\begin{align*}
    &\left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\cdot\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}  + \frac{n}{\gamma} - (1-\epsilon) n\frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} + 1 + n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})}\\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\beta  + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 \\
    &= \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}\cdot \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{c_{min}}\\
    & = \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 - \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c_{min}}\\
    &\leq \frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} 
\end{align*}

Thus, we proved for the inductive step,
\[f(S_{j+1}) \geq \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta \left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} \right)\]

        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) f(S_j) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) \right]}_{\mbox{\it by induction hypothesis}} \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \  - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \\
        &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT}) + \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \left(   1- \prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right)f({\rm OPT})  \\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -\left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) 2\delta(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma})   - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\left[\prod_{s=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]f({\rm OPT})\\
        & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  \\
        &= \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) -2\delta \left[ \left(1-\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_{j+1})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+\frac{n}{\gamma}) +  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_{j+1})}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $f(S_{j+1})$, apply Lemma 19 and the hypothesis.

nodes.name: Bound the error term
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the accumulated error term.

nodes.name: Conclude step
nodes.statement:
Thus, we proved for the inductive step,
\[f(S_{j+1}) \geq \left( 1- \prod_{s=1}^{j+1} (1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_s)}{c({\rm OPT})} )   \right) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta \left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} + \frac{n}{\gamma} \right)\]
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step established.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10
nodes.statement:
Let $S_\ell$ be the set at the termination of Algorithm \ref{alg:up}. We divide the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} into two cases based on the relationship between $A$ and $c(S_\ell)$. 

    \textbf{Case 1}: $\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell) < A$.
    
    
    
    Consider each element $u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_\ell$ that was not included into $S_\ell$; such an element can be categorized into two sets $O_1$ and $O_2$ with corresponding reasons:

     $\bullet$~ \textit{$O_1$ is the set of elements for which the line 7 condition was not satisfied.\ }
     
     The density of these elements is $\leq \gamma$ at some point before the algorithm ends. Therefore, for $u \in O_1$, if $\frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)}$ is the density (key) of $u$ the last time it appears in the priority queue, then 
     \[ \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma\]
     By the definition of approximate oracles,
     \[ \frac{f(u|S_\ell) - 2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u) - 2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma \]
     Then we have for $u \in O_1$
    \begin{equation} f(u|S_\ell) \leq \gamma c(u) + 2\delta       
    \end{equation}
        
    
    $\bullet$~ \textit{$O_2$ is the set of elements for which the line 18 condition was not satisfied.\ }\\
    In other words, these elements  have been considered for $\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma\epsilon}}{\epsilon} $ times. Note that for any $u \in O_2$, the initial density of $u$ in the priority queue is $\frac{f(u)}{c(u)}$. Then, suppose $\frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)}$ is the key of $u$ the last time it existed in $PQ$. Therefore, as $S_u \subseteq S_\ell$ we have 
    \[\frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}  \frac{\Tilde{f}(u)}{c(u)}\]
    By the definition of approximate oracles (Def. \ref{def:approximate}), we derive both terms in the above inequality
    \[\frac{f(u|S_\ell)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u))} \]
    
    \[\frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{\Tilde{f}(u)}{c(u)} \leq  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{f(u)+\delta}{c(u)}\]
    
    Therefore, by combining the above two inequalities, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \frac{f(u|S_\ell)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{f(u)+\delta}{c(u)}
    \end{equation*}
    Then, for every $u \in O_2$,
    \begin{align}
        f(u|S_\ell) &\leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} [ f(u) + \delta ] + 2\delta \nonumber\\
        & = (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} f(u) + 2\delta +  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \delta \end{align}
    

    Therefore, we derive
    \begin{align*}
        &f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \\
        &\leq f({\rm OPT} \cup S_\ell)-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to monotonicity of $f$}\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \quad \quad\quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it due to Definition~\ref{def:weak-sub}}\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} f(u|S_\ell)+\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\right)-c({\rm OPT})\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} f(u|S_\ell)+\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\right)-\sum_{u \in O_1} c(u) \quad \quad\quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it as $c$ is modular}\\
        &=\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{1}{\gamma} f(u|S_\ell) - c(u)\right)~~+~~\frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell) \quad \quad \quad\quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it from Eq. (\ref{eq:o1-approx})}\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}f(u) + 2\delta +  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \delta \right] \quad \quad\quad\quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it from Eq. (\ref{eq:o2-approx})}\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1 \cup O_2} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right]\\
        &\leq \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right]\\
        
        
        
        
        &\leq \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~  \epsilon \delta+ \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) 
    \end{align*}
    To get the last inequality, we need to show the following holds
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right] &\leq   \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to $1-\epsilon \leq \frac{1}{1+\epsilon}$}\\
        &\leq  \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\log (1+\epsilon)}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to $\epsilon \leq \log (1+\epsilon)$}\\
        &=    \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\log_{1+\epsilon} \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \\
        &=   \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} \frac{\gamma \epsilon}{n} \Big(f(u) + \delta \Big)\\
        &\leq  \epsilon \delta+ \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) 
    \end{align*}
    
    The last inequality holds because $O_2 \subseteq {\rm OPT}$, $|{\rm OPT}| \leq n$ and $f(u) \leq f({\rm OPT})$.
     Thus, rearranging the above inequality and combining it with the condition for Case 1 ($0< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A-c(S_\ell)$), we obtain
     \[ 
     f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) - \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) - \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma}  - \epsilon \delta \leq 0 \leq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A-c(S_\ell) 
     \]
     
     So, 
     \begin{align*}
         &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_\ell)-c(S_\ell)\\
         &\geq (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} - \epsilon \delta\\
         &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
     \end{align*}
     
    
    {This concludes the proof of the theorem for case 1}. \hfill $\Box$


\textbf{Case 2}: $\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell) \geq A$. 

In this case, there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that:
    \begin{equation}
        c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t) \end{equation}
Denote $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$. 
Consider $j \in [1, t-1]$, we further divide Case 2 into two sub-cases: (2.1) and (2.2), where for some $j \in [1,t-1]$, sub-case 2.1 corresponds to $f(S_{j}) \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$  and sub-case 2.2 corresponds to $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$ for all $j \in [1,t-1]$.

\textbf{Case 2.1}: For some $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

Note that Algorithm~\ref{alg:up} outputs $\Tilde{S} = arg\,max_{S_i, i \in [n]} f(S_i)-c(S_i)$.
Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
f(\Tilde{S}) - c(\Tilde{S}) & > f(S_j) - c(S_j) \\
&\geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}  \quad\quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it follows from  condition in Case 2.1 and Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})} \\
& \geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \xi
\end{align*}


This concludes the proof of the theorem for sub-case 2.1.  \hfill $\Box$

\textbf{Case 2.2}: For all $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

For the \textbf{sub-case 2.2}, as illustrated in the proof-path, we have already
proved the Lemmas~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx} and \ref{lem:f-Si-approx}. We will now prove
the necessary properties conditioned on the sub-case 2.2. 

\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$),
the following holds: 
                
 \[\forall~j \in [1, t-1]: ~c(v_j) \leq c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{claim}


\begin{proof}
We prove this claim by contradiction. Assume there exist some $j \in [1, t-1]$ that $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$. Also, recall that as per the condition in sub-case 2.2, we have
\begin{align}
    &f(S_j) < \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi \nonumber\\ 
\Leftrightarrow &~~ f({\rm OPT}) > \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Big(f(S_j)+\xi\Big) > f(S_j) >f(S_{j-1}) \end{align}


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
    f(S_j)&= f(S_{j-1}) + f(v_j|S_{j-1})\\
    &\geq f(S_{j-1}) + \underbrace{\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)}_{\mbox{\it  follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}} \\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT}) + \Big[ 1- \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq { \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT})} + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ 1- \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= {\gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big]f({\rm OPT})} \\ &\quad \quad - \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) \\ &\quad\quad + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] \big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big)- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the assumption $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$ and Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and $\frac{c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \leq \beta'$}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - \xi
\end{align*}

The last inequality hold from $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ and $\beta>0$.
Note that, using the assumption, we have concluded that $f(S_j) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$, which contradicts the premise of the claim (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})). Therefore, the assumption is incorrect, and the claim holds.
\end{proof}
            
\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), define $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, the following holds: 
\[ \forall~j \in [1, t-1]:~ c(v_t) > B_{t-1}\]
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}

\begin{align*}
c(v_t) &= c(S_t) - c(S_{t-1})\\
&\geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A- c(S_{t-1}) \quad\quad\quad {\mbox{\it follows from the case 2 condition Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})}} \\
& =  \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}\big(A-\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1})\big) \\
&\geq  A- \gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1}) =  B_{t-1}
\end{align*}


\end{proof}


\begin{lemma} Under the case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), the following
holds:
for all $j\in [1,t-1]$,
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, then
\[ 
   f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \leq \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) 
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


We divide this proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ For \textbf{$B_j > c({\rm OPT})$}, the lemma holds immediately.

\smallskip
$\bullet$ We focus on \textbf{$B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$}.

\begin{align*}
    & \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
        &= \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)f(S_{j}) + \frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &\geq  \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{k=1}^{j}  \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:f-Si-approx}}} + \displaystyle\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &=f({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\left(\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &=\left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]
        &=\left( 1- \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{f({\rm OPT})} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}














    
\end{proof}

   
\begin{corollary} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$), the following holds: 
for all $j \in  [1, t-1],$ 
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$ then \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}


   Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately. 
   Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}
       f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &
        <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
         &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \Big(\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}
   
    The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{proof}

            
            

The following lemma discharges the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for the sub-case 2.2. 


\begin{lemma} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$),
the following holds:
    \[f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right) \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
    &=f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  +  f(S_{t-1})-c(S_t) \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}} \\
    & = \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi \right] +f(S_{t-1})- {\Big(c(S_{t-1})+c(v_t)\Big)} \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it denote $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)$}\\    
    &= \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}
\end{align*}
The last equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

\smallskip
Proceeding further, 

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}\\
    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) 
\end{align*}


Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

\end{proof}

This concludes the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for Case 2.2. 

\medskip
\begin{lemma} The time complexity of Algorithm \ref{alg:up} is 
    
    $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon} \log \frac{n}{\epsilon \gamma})$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
    As per line 17 of Algorithm \ref{alg:up}, every element can be considered for adding to the solution set for at most $\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}$ times. Each such consideration involves one oracle call to the function $f$. Therefore, the total number of oracle calls is $\mathcal{O}(\frac{n}{\epsilon} \log \frac{n}{\epsilon \gamma})$. 
    
\end{proof}

nodes.name: Split on $A$ vs $c(S_\ell)$
nodes.statement: Let $S_\ell$ be the set at the termination of Algorithm \ref{alg:up}. We divide the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} into two cases based on the relationship between $A$ and $c(S_\ell)$.
nodes.statement_short: Split into two cases by $A$ vs $c(S_\ell)$.

nodes.name: Case 1
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 1}: $\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell) < A$.
    
    
    
    Consider each element $u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_\ell$ that was not included into $S_\ell$; such an element can be categorized into two sets $O_1$ and $O_2$ with corresponding reasons:

     $\bullet$~ \textit{$O_1$ is the set of elements for which the line 7 condition was not satisfied.\ }
     
     The density of these elements is $\leq \gamma$ at some point before the algorithm ends. Therefore, for $u \in O_1$, if $\frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)}$ is the density (key) of $u$ the last time it appears in the priority queue, then 
     \[ \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma\]
     By the definition of approximate oracles,
     \[ \frac{f(u|S_\ell) - 2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u) - 2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq \gamma \]
     Then we have for $u \in O_1$
    \begin{equation} f(u|S_\ell) \leq \gamma c(u) + 2\delta       
    \end{equation}
        
    
    $\bullet$~ \textit{$O_2$ is the set of elements for which the line 18 condition was not satisfied.\ }\\
    In other words, these elements  have been considered for $\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma\epsilon}}{\epsilon} $ times. Note that for any $u \in O_2$, the initial density of $u$ in the priority queue is $\frac{f(u)}{c(u)}$. Then, suppose $\frac{f(u|S_u)}{c(u)}$ is the key of $u$ the last time it existed in $PQ$. Therefore, as $S_u \subseteq S_\ell$ we have 
    \[\frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}  \frac{\Tilde{f}(u)}{c(u)}\]
    By the definition of approximate oracles (Def. \ref{def:approximate}), we derive both terms in the above inequality
    \[\frac{f(u|S_\ell)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{f(u|S_u)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq \frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u))} \]
    
    \[\frac{\Tilde{f}(u|S_u)}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{\Tilde{f}(u)}{c(u)} \leq  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{f(u)+\delta}{c(u)}\]
    
    Therefore, by combining the above two inequalities, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \frac{f(u|S_\ell)-2\delta}{c(u)} \leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \cdot \frac{f(u)+\delta}{c(u)}
    \end{equation*}
    Then, for every $u \in O_2$,
    \begin{align}
        f(u|S_\ell) &\leq (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} [ f(u) + \delta ] + 2\delta \nonumber\\
        & = (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} f(u) + 2\delta +  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \delta \end{align}
    

    Therefore, we derive
    \begin{align*}
        &f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \\
        &\leq f({\rm OPT} \cup S_\ell)-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to monotonicity of $f$}\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in {\rm OPT} \setminus S_{\ell}} f(u|S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) \quad \quad\quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it due to Definition~\ref{def:weak-sub}}\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} f(u|S_\ell)+\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\right)-c({\rm OPT})\\
        &\leq \frac{1}{\gamma}\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} f(u|S_\ell)+\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\right)-\sum_{u \in O_1} c(u) \quad \quad\quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it as $c$ is modular}\\
        &=\left(\sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{1}{\gamma} f(u|S_\ell) - c(u)\right)~~+~~\frac{1}{\gamma}\sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell)\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} f(u|S_\ell) \quad \quad \quad\quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it from Eq. (\ref{eq:o1-approx})}\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}f(u) + 2\delta +  (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}} \delta \right] \quad \quad\quad\quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it from Eq. (\ref{eq:o2-approx})}\\
        &\leq \sum_{u \in O_1 \cup O_2} \frac{2\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right]\\
        &\leq \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~ \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right]\\
        
        
        
        
        &\leq \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} ~~+~~  \epsilon \delta+ \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) 
    \end{align*}
    To get the last inequality, we need to show the following holds
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2}\left[ (1-\epsilon)^{\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \right] &\leq   \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to $1-\epsilon \leq \frac{1}{1+\epsilon}$}\\
        &\leq  \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\log (1+\epsilon)}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \quad \quad\quad \quad \mbox{\it due to $\epsilon \leq \log (1+\epsilon)$}\\
        &=    \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} (1+\epsilon)^{-\log_{1+\epsilon} \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}\Big(f(u) + \delta \Big) \\
        &=   \frac{1}{\gamma} \sum_{u \in O_2} \frac{\gamma \epsilon}{n} \Big(f(u) + \delta \Big)\\
        &\leq  \epsilon \delta+ \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) 
    \end{align*}
    
    The last inequality holds because $O_2 \subseteq {\rm OPT}$, $|{\rm OPT}| \leq n$ and $f(u) \leq f({\rm OPT})$.
     Thus, rearranging the above inequality and combining it with the condition for Case 1 ($0< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A-c(S_\ell)$), we obtain
     \[ 
     f({\rm OPT})-f(S_\ell)-c({\rm OPT}) - \epsilon f({\rm OPT}) - \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma}  - \epsilon \delta \leq 0 \leq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A-c(S_\ell) 
     \]
     
     So, 
     \begin{align*}
         &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_\ell)-c(S_\ell)\\
         &\geq (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - \frac{2n\delta}{\gamma} - \epsilon \delta\\
         &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
     \end{align*}
     
    
    {This concludes the proof of the theorem for case 1}. \hfill $\Box$
