nodes.name: Case 2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 2}: $\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell) \geq A$. 

In this case, there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that:
    \begin{equation}
        c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t) \end{equation}
Denote $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$. 
Consider $j \in [1, t-1]$, we further divide Case 2 into two sub-cases: (2.1) and (2.2), where for some $j \in [1,t-1]$, sub-case 2.1 corresponds to $f(S_{j}) \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$  and sub-case 2.2 corresponds to $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$ for all $j \in [1,t-1]$.

\textbf{Case 2.1}: For some $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

Note that Algorithm~\ref{alg:up} outputs $\Tilde{S} = arg\,max_{S_i, i \in [n]} f(S_i)-c(S_i)$.
Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
f(\Tilde{S}) - c(\Tilde{S}) & > f(S_j) - c(S_j) \\
&\geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}  \quad\quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it follows from  condition in Case 2.1 and Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})} \\
& \geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \xi
\end{align*}


This concludes the proof of the theorem for sub-case 2.1.  \hfill $\Box$

\textbf{Case 2.2}: For all $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

For the \textbf{sub-case 2.2}, as illustrated in the proof-path, we have already
proved the Lemmas~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx} and \ref{lem:f-Si-approx}. We will now prove
the necessary properties conditioned on the sub-case 2.2. 

\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$),
the following holds: 
                
 \[\forall~j \in [1, t-1]: ~c(v_j) \leq c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{claim}


\begin{proof}
We prove this claim by contradiction. Assume there exist some $j \in [1, t-1]$ that $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$. Also, recall that as per the condition in sub-case 2.2, we have
\begin{align}
    &f(S_j) < \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi \nonumber\\ 
\Leftrightarrow &~~ f({\rm OPT}) > \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Big(f(S_j)+\xi\Big) > f(S_j) >f(S_{j-1}) \end{align}


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
    f(S_j)&= f(S_{j-1}) + f(v_j|S_{j-1})\\
    &\geq f(S_{j-1}) + \underbrace{\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)}_{\mbox{\it  follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}} \\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT}) + \Big[ 1- \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq { \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT})} + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ 1- \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= {\gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big]f({\rm OPT})} \\ &\quad \quad - \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) \\ &\quad\quad + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] \big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big)- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the assumption $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$ and Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and $\frac{c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \leq \beta'$}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - \xi
\end{align*}

The last inequality hold from $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ and $\beta>0$.
Note that, using the assumption, we have concluded that $f(S_j) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$, which contradicts the premise of the claim (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})). Therefore, the assumption is incorrect, and the claim holds.
\end{proof}
            
\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), define $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, the following holds: 
\[ \forall~j \in [1, t-1]:~ c(v_t) > B_{t-1}\]
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}

\begin{align*}
c(v_t) &= c(S_t) - c(S_{t-1})\\
&\geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A- c(S_{t-1}) \quad\quad\quad {\mbox{\it follows from the case 2 condition Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})}} \\
& =  \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}\big(A-\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1})\big) \\
&\geq  A- \gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1}) =  B_{t-1}
\end{align*}


\end{proof}


\begin{lemma} Under the case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), the following
holds:
for all $j\in [1,t-1]$,
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, then
\[ 
   f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \leq \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) 
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


We divide this proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ For \textbf{$B_j > c({\rm OPT})$}, the lemma holds immediately.

\smallskip
$\bullet$ We focus on \textbf{$B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$}.

\begin{align*}
    & \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
        &= \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)f(S_{j}) + \frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &\geq  \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{k=1}^{j}  \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:f-Si-approx}}} + \displaystyle\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &=f({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\left(\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &=\left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]
        &=\left( 1- \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{f({\rm OPT})} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}














    
\end{proof}

   
\begin{corollary} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$), the following holds: 
for all $j \in  [1, t-1],$ 
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$ then \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}


   Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately. 
   Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}
       f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &
        <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
         &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \Big(\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}
   
    The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{proof}

            
            

The following lemma discharges the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for the sub-case 2.2. 


\begin{lemma} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$),
the following holds:
    \[f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right) \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
    &=f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  +  f(S_{t-1})-c(S_t) \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}} \\
    & = \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi \right] +f(S_{t-1})- {\Big(c(S_{t-1})+c(v_t)\Big)} \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it denote $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)$}\\    
    &= \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}
\end{align*}
The last equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

\smallskip
Proceeding further, 

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}\\
    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) 
\end{align*}


Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

\end{proof}

This concludes the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for Case 2.2.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_\ell)\ge A$ with sub-cases.

nodes.name: Threshold index and $\xi$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $t$ and $\xi$; define sub-cases 2.1, 2.2.

nodes.name: Case 2.1
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 2.1}: For some $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

Note that Algorithm~\ref{alg:up} outputs $\Tilde{S} = arg\,max_{S_i, i \in [n]} f(S_i)-c(S_i)$.
Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
f(\Tilde{S}) - c(\Tilde{S}) & > f(S_j) - c(S_j) \\
&\geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}  \quad\quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it follows from  condition in Case 2.1 and Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})} \\
& \geq  \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\frac{A}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} - \xi
\end{align*}


This concludes the proof of the theorem for sub-case 2.1.  \hfill $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Some early $S_j$ is already good enough.

nodes.name: Case 2.2
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case 2.2}: For all $j\in [1,t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$.

For the \textbf{sub-case 2.2}, as illustrated in the proof-path, we have already
proved the Lemmas~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx} and \ref{lem:f-Si-approx}. We will now prove
the necessary properties conditioned on the sub-case 2.2. 

\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$),
the following holds: 
                
 \[\forall~j \in [1, t-1]: ~c(v_j) \leq c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{claim}


\begin{proof}
We prove this claim by contradiction. Assume there exist some $j \in [1, t-1]$ that $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$. Also, recall that as per the condition in sub-case 2.2, we have
\begin{align}
    &f(S_j) < \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi \nonumber\\ 
\Leftrightarrow &~~ f({\rm OPT}) > \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Big(f(S_j)+\xi\Big) > f(S_j) >f(S_{j-1}) \end{align}


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
    f(S_j)&= f(S_{j-1}) + f(v_j|S_{j-1})\\
    &\geq f(S_{j-1}) + \underbrace{\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)}_{\mbox{\it  follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}} \\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT}) + \Big[ 1- \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq { \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT})} + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ 1- \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= {\gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big]f({\rm OPT})} \\ &\quad \quad - \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) \\ &\quad\quad + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] \big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big)- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the assumption $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$ and Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and $\frac{c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \leq \beta'$}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - \xi
\end{align*}

The last inequality hold from $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ and $\beta>0$.
Note that, using the assumption, we have concluded that $f(S_j) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$, which contradicts the premise of the claim (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})). Therefore, the assumption is incorrect, and the claim holds.
\end{proof}
            
\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), define $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, the following holds: 
\[ \forall~j \in [1, t-1]:~ c(v_t) > B_{t-1}\]
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}

\begin{align*}
c(v_t) &= c(S_t) - c(S_{t-1})\\
&\geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A- c(S_{t-1}) \quad\quad\quad {\mbox{\it follows from the case 2 condition Eq.~(\ref{eq:th1-case2-approx})}} \\
& =  \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}\big(A-\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1})\big) \\
&\geq  A- \gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{t-1}) =  B_{t-1}
\end{align*}


\end{proof}


\begin{lemma} Under the case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), the following
holds:
for all $j\in [1,t-1]$,
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, then
\[ 
   f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \leq \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) 
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


We divide this proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ For \textbf{$B_j > c({\rm OPT})$}, the lemma holds immediately.

\smallskip
$\bullet$ We focus on \textbf{$B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$}.

\begin{align*}
    & \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
        &= \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)f(S_{j}) + \frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &\geq  \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{k=1}^{j}  \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:f-Si-approx}}} + \displaystyle\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &=f({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\left(\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &=\left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]
        &=\left( 1- \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{f({\rm OPT})} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}














    
\end{proof}

   
\begin{corollary} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$), the following holds: 
for all $j \in  [1, t-1],$ 
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$ then \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}


   Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately. 
   Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}
       f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &
        <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
         &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \Big(\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}
   
    The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{proof}

            
            

The following lemma discharges the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for the sub-case 2.2. 


\begin{lemma} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$),
the following holds:
    \[f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right) \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
    &=f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  +  f(S_{t-1})-c(S_t) \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}} \\
    & = \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi \right] +f(S_{t-1})- {\Big(c(S_{t-1})+c(v_t)\Big)} \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it denote $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)$}\\    
    &= \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}
\end{align*}
The last equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

\smallskip
Proceeding further, 

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}\\
    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) 
\end{align*}


Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

\end{proof}

This concludes the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for Case 2.2.

For the \textbf{sub-case 2.2}, as illustrated in the proof-path, we have already

nodes.name: Claim 21 and its proof
nodes.statement:
\begin{claim} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$),
the following holds: 
                
 \[\forall~j \in [1, t-1]: ~c(v_j) \leq c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{claim}


\begin{proof}
We prove this claim by contradiction. Assume there exist some $j \in [1, t-1]$ that $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$. Also, recall that as per the condition in sub-case 2.2, we have
\begin{align}
    &f(S_j) < \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi \nonumber\\ 
\Leftrightarrow &~~ f({\rm OPT}) > \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Big(f(S_j)+\xi\Big) > f(S_j) >f(S_{j-1}) \end{align}


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
    f(S_j)&= f(S_{j-1}) + f(v_j|S_{j-1})\\
    &\geq f(S_{j-1}) + \underbrace{\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)}_{\mbox{\it  follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}} \\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT}) + \Big[ 1- \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq { \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT})} + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ 1- \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= {\gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big]f({\rm OPT})} \\ &\quad \quad - \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) \\ &\quad\quad + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] \big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big)- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the assumption $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$ and Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and $\frac{c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \leq \beta'$}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - \xi
\end{align*}

The last inequality hold from $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ and $\beta>0$.
Note that, using the assumption, we have concluded that $f(S_j) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$, which contradicts the premise of the claim (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})). Therefore, the assumption is incorrect, and the claim holds.
\end{proof}

nodes.name: Lemma 23 and its proof
nodes.statement:
\begin{lemma} Under the case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), the following
holds:
for all $j\in [1,t-1]$,
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, then
\[ 
   f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \leq \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) 
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


We divide this proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ For \textbf{$B_j > c({\rm OPT})$}, the lemma holds immediately.

\smallskip
$\bullet$ We focus on \textbf{$B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$}.

\begin{align*}
    & \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
        &= \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)f(S_{j}) + \frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &\geq  \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{k=1}^{j}  \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:f-Si-approx}}} + \displaystyle\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &=f({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\left(\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &=\left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]
        &=\left( 1- \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{f({\rm OPT})} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}














    
\end{proof}

nodes.name: Corollary 24 and its proof
nodes.statement:
\begin{corollary} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$), the following holds: 
for all $j \in  [1, t-1],$ 
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$ then \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}


   Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately. 
   Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}
       f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &
        <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
         &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \Big(\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}
   
    The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
\end{proof}

nodes.name: Lemma 25 closes Case 2.2
nodes.statement:
The following lemma discharges the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for the sub-case 2.2. 


\begin{lemma} Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$),
the following holds:
    \[f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right) \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}


Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
    &=f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  +  f(S_{t-1})-c(S_t) \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}} \\
    & = \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi \right] +f(S_{t-1})- {\Big(c(S_{t-1})+c(v_t)\Big)} \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it denote $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)$}\\    
    &= \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}
\end{align*}
The last equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

\smallskip
Proceeding further, 

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}\\
    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) 
\end{align*}


Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

\end{proof}

This concludes the proof for Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} for Case 2.2.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 21
nodes.statement:
We prove this claim by contradiction. Assume there exist some $j \in [1, t-1]$ that $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$. Also, recall that as per the condition in sub-case 2.2, we have
\begin{align}
    &f(S_j) < \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi \nonumber\\ 
\Leftrightarrow &~~ f({\rm OPT}) > \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)} \Big(f(S_j)+\xi\Big) > f(S_j) >f(S_{j-1}) \end{align}


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
    f(S_j)&= f(S_{j-1}) + f(v_j|S_{j-1})\\
    &\geq f(S_{j-1}) + \underbrace{\gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)}_{\mbox{\it  follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}}} \\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT}) + \Big[ 1- \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq { \gamma(1-\epsilon)\frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} f({\rm OPT})} + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ 1- \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big]f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= {\gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big]f({\rm OPT})} \\ &\quad \quad - \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] f(S_{j-1})- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &= \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) \\ &\quad\quad + \gamma(1-\epsilon)\Big[ \frac{c(v_j)}{c({\rm OPT})} - 1 \Big] \big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j-1}) \big)- 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the assumption $c(v_j)>c({\rm OPT})$ and Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$ and $\frac{c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \leq \beta'$}\\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) - \xi
\end{align*}

The last inequality hold from $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ and $\beta>0$.
Note that, using the assumption, we have concluded that $f(S_j) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT}) -\xi$, which contradicts the premise of the claim (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:case2.2-approx})). Therefore, the assumption is incorrect, and the claim holds.

and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), define $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$, the following holds: 
\[ \forall~j \in [1, t-1]:~ c(v_t) > B_{t-1}\]

and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$), the following
holds:
for all $j\in [1,t-1]$,

\]
conclusions: f({\rm OPT}) - c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \leq \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 23
nodes.statement:
We divide this proof into two cases.

$\bullet$ For \textbf{$B_j > c({\rm OPT})$}, the lemma holds immediately.

\smallskip
$\bullet$ We focus on \textbf{$B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$}.

\begin{align*}
    & \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
        &= \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)f(S_{j}) + \frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &\geq  \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\underbrace{\left[\left(   1- \prod_{k=1}^{j}  \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)   \right) f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:f-Si-approx}}} + \displaystyle\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}f({\rm OPT})\\
        &=f({\rm OPT}) - \displaystyle\left(\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &=\left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\prod_{k=1}^{j} \left(1- \gamma(1-\epsilon) \frac{c(v_k)}{c({\rm OPT})} \right) \right)f({\rm OPT}) - \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]
        &=\left( 1- \frac{c({\rm OPT})}{f({\rm OPT})} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: As Lemma 6 with Lemma 20 in place of Lemma 3: product-sum inequality and $(1-c/t)^t\le e^{-c}$, carrying the $\delta$ term.

\begin{align*}

We proceed with the following known inequality: for any

Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that,

$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case. 

Therefore, by applying Eq.~(\ref{eq:prodsum-approx}), we derive the following

\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)
\end{align*}


Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]

        &= f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)

nodes.name: Product-sum inequality
nodes.statement:
We proceed with the following known inequality: for any 
\[x_1, x_2, \cdots, x_n, y \in \mathbb{R}^{+} \mbox{ and } x_i \leq y \mbox{ for } i \leq n\]
\begin{equation}
1-\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac{x_i}{y}\right) \geq 1-\left(1-\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{n y}\right)^n \end{equation}
Consider $\forall k\in [1,j], x_k = \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k)$, $x_{k+1} = B_j$ and $y = c({\rm OPT})$. Note that, 
$\forall k\in [1,j], \gamma(1-\epsilon) c(v_k) \leq c({\rm OPT})$, which follows from Claim~\ref{claim:single-cost-approx} and 
$\gamma(1-\epsilon) \leq 1$. Also, $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$ follows from the condition for this case.

nodes.name: Exponential bound
nodes.statement:
Since $B_j \leq c({\rm OPT})$, $0 \leq \left(1-\frac{B_j}{c({\rm OPT})}\right)\leq 1$. Proceeding further, 


\begin{align*}
    &\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) \\
    &\geq \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{B_j+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left(1- \frac{A-\gamma(1-\epsilon)c(S_j)+\gamma(1-\epsilon)\cdot \sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k)}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT})- 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\\
    & \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it follows from the definition of $B_j$} \\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{A}{(j+1)\cdot c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\quad\quad\quad\mbox{\it as $\sum_{k=1}^{j}c(v_k) = c(S_j)$}\\[1em]
        &= \left( 1- \displaystyle\left( 1- \frac{1}{j+1}\cdot \ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})} \right)^{j+1} \right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \mbox{\it as $A=c({\rm OPT})\ln\frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}$} \\[1em]
        &\geq \left(1- e^{-\ln \frac{f({\rm OPT})}{c({\rm OPT})}}\right)f({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \quad \quad \quad \mbox{\it as $(1- \frac{c}{t} )^t \leq e^{-c}$ for any positive $t$} \\[1em]

nodes.name: Gap lower bound (Case 2.2, approximate)
nodes.statement:
Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT}) - \xi$), the following holds: 
for all $j \in  [1, t-1],$ 
if $B_j=A-\gamma(1-\epsilon) c(S_{j})$ then \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
nodes.label: col:lower-opt-approx

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 24
nodes.statement:
Note that, for the case $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately. 
   Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}
       f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j}) &
        <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
         &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \Big(\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}
   
    The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]
nodes.statement_short: If the theorem bound fails at $S_j$, Lemma 23 and $\xi$'s size yield the gap bound after rearranging.

            \geq \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$ , Theorem~\ref{th:unconstrained-approx} holds immediately.

Hence, we consider the case where $f(S_{j}) -c(S_{j})
            <\gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A -\xi$. 
   
   \begin{align*}

        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}\Big(A -\gamma (1-\epsilon)c(S_{j})\Big) -\xi\\
        &=\gamma (1-\epsilon)\Big(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})\Big)- c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j -\xi\\
        &\leq \gamma (1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j})+2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)\right]}_{\mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}}  - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  -\xi \\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j  + \underbrace{2\delta(\beta ~+~ \frac{n}{\gamma}) ~~-~~ \xi}_{\mbox{\it $<0$ since $\xi = 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)$ }}\\
        &\leq \displaystyle\frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} +f(S_{j}) - c(S_{j}) - \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j
   \end{align*}

nodes.name: Rearrange
nodes.statement:
The above inequality implies:
    \[ \frac{B_j(f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{j}))}{c({\rm OPT})} \geq \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}B_j \]

    Rearranging the term concludes the proof of the corollary.
    \[f({\rm OPT}) -f(S_{j}) \geq \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}c({\rm OPT})\]

nodes.name: Lower bound on $f(S_t)-c(S_t)$ (Case 2.2, approximate)
nodes.statement:
Under the Case 2.2 (i.e., 
there exist $t\in[1, \ell]$ such that
$c(S_{t-1})< \frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)} A  \leq c(S_t)$
and for all $j\in[1, t-1]$, $f(S_{j}) < \gamma (1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-\xi$),
the following holds:
    \[f(S_t)-c(S_t) \geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right) \]
nodes.label: lem:unconstrained-h_St-approx

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 25
nodes.statement:
Consider $v_t$ the element added to $S_{t-1}$.
\begin{align*}
    & f(S_t)-c(S_t) \\
    &=f(v_t|S_{t-1})+f(S_{t-1})-{c(S_t)}\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)\right]  +  f(S_{t-1})-c(S_t) \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it due to Lemma~\ref{lem:marginal-gain-approx}} \\
    & = \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi \right] +f(S_{t-1})- {\Big(c(S_{t-1})+c(v_t)\Big)} \quad\quad\quad \mbox{\it denote $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_t)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right)$}\\    
    &= \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}
\end{align*}
The last equality follows from the definition of  $B_{t-1} = A-\gamma (1-\epsilon) c(S_{t-1})$.

\smallskip
Proceeding further, 

\begin{align*}
    &f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
    &\geq \left[\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}+c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big ( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \Big ) - \phi\right]  +f(S_{t-1})- {\left(\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}(A-B_{t-1})+c(v_t)\right)}\\
    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) 
\end{align*}


Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

    &\geq  {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \Big( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})\Big)}+ f(S_{t-1})    + {\gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) }\\
        &\quad\quad - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\left(c(v_t)-\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}B_{t-1}\right)\\
    &\geq  \gamma(1-\epsilon)  \underbrace{\left[\displaystyle\frac{B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) + f(S_{t-1})\right]}_{} ~~+~~ \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{c(v_t)-B_{t-1}}{c({\rm OPT})} \left( f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) \right) \\
        &\quad\quad- \phi- {\displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A-\Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]}\\  
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) \underbrace{\left(f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) \right)}_{\mbox{\it apply Lemma~\ref{lem:h-upper-bound-approx}}} ~~-~~ \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - \gamma(1-\epsilon)2\delta\left(\frac{\beta}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \Big[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\Big]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right) \\
    &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon) f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT}) - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi - \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}A \\
        &\quad\quad + \left[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}\right]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1}) }{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)

Note that, in Claim \ref{claim:cost-St-approx}, we have established $c(v_t)\geq B_{t-1}$. Furthermore, from Corollary \ref{col:lower-opt-approx}, we know
$f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_j) \geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{\gamma(1-\epsilon)}{c({\rm OPT})}$. Therefore, 
\[
[c(v_t)-B_{t-1}]\left( \gamma(1-\epsilon) \displaystyle\frac{f({\rm OPT}) - f(S_{t-1})}{c({\rm OPT})} -1 \right)
\]
is non-negative. Hence, 



If we denote $\beta' = \frac{c_{max}}{c({\rm OPT})}$, then $\phi = 2\delta  \left( 1+n\frac{(1-\epsilon)c(v_i)}{ c({\rm OPT})} \right) \leq 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)$
\begin{align*}
   &f(\Tilde{S})-c(\Tilde{S}) \geq f(S_t)-c(S_t)\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right)  - \phi\\
   &\geq \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma}\right) - 2\delta  \left( 1+n(1-\epsilon)\beta' \right)\\
   &= \gamma(1-\epsilon)f({\rm OPT})-c({\rm OPT})-\frac{1}{\gamma (1-\epsilon)}A - 2\delta\left(\beta+ \frac{n}{\gamma} + 1 + n(1-\epsilon)\beta'\right)
\end{align*}

nodes.statement: As per line 17 of Algorithm \ref{alg:up}, every element can be considered for adding to the solution set for at most $\frac{\log \frac{n}{\gamma \epsilon}}{\epsilon}$ times.
